extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and developers working on AI-generated narratives and story-coherence evaluation
extracted.subtask_short: story coherence evaluation for AI narratives
extracted.subtask_description: A framework and evaluation approach for detecting, retrieving, and resolving narrative inconsistencies in large-language-model–generated stories to improve coherence and emotional depth. Focuses on methods (tracking item statuses, episode summarization, RAG) and experimental comparison to baseline GPT models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story coherence (consistency and stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain coherence throughout AI-generated stories; specifically improve the 'consistency and stability of narrative coherence' across episodes and the whole narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper frames coherence as a primary target of SCORE and reports experimental results showing SCORE 'significantly improves the consistency and stability of narrative coherence compared to baseline GPT models.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional depth across the narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve or enhance emotional depth throughout stories generated by LLMs so that affect and emotional arcs remain engaging and coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract highlights 'emotional depth' alongside coherence as a challenge for LLM-generated narratives, indicating systems should track and maintain emotional content over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and resolving narrative inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify contradictions, continuity errors, or logical lapses within the narrative and take actions to resolve them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SCORE is presented as 'designed to detect and resolve narrative inconsistencies.' The framework operationalizes detection+resolution rather than only post-hoc scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking key item statuses (episodic state tracking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the statuses of key items (e.g., characters, objects, facts, events) across episodes to maintain continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper describes 'tracking key item statuses' as a component of SCORE that supports coherence maintenance by keeping an updated episodic state or memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating episode summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce concise summaries of episodes to capture salient events and states that can be used for retrieval and consistency checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SCORE 'generat[es] episode summaries' which are used alongside item tracking to provide compact representations for retrieval and reasoning about the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to identify related episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use retrieval methods to find and reference related prior episodes or facts when producing new text to ensure coherence and avoid contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework 'uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach to identify related episodes and enhance the overall story structure,' implying retrieval relevance and effective use of retrieved context are evaluation dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing overall story structure (global narrative organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the macro-level organization of the story—episode ordering, pacing, and the logical progression of plot—so the narrative reads as a cohesive whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SCORE is claimed to 'enhance the overall story structure' by combining tracking, summarization, and retrieval; global structure is thus an intended evaluation target beyond local sentence-level fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust evaluation via comparative experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirically evaluate methods by comparing coherence-related metrics against baseline models (e.g., GPT variants) to demonstrate improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract emphasizes 'experimental results from testing multiple LLM-generated stories' and that SCORE 'significantly improves' coherence relative to baselines, indicating comparative experimental validation is part of the rubric for success.
